content_metadata.description: An educational video explaining the structure and properties of diamonds and other covalent network solids. The video provides insights into carbon allotropes and their characteristics.

qAndA.answer: All of diamond's electrons are involved in strong covalent bonds, leaving none free to carry a charge.
qAndA.question: What makes diamond a good electrical insulator?
What is the name of the arrangement in which each carbon atom is bonded to four other carbon atoms in a diamond?

qAndA.answer: Graphite has delocalized electrons that are free to move and carry electrical charge, while diamond's electrons are all tightly bound in covalent bonds.
qAndA.question: Why does graphite conduct electricity while diamond does not?

qAndA.answer: An allotrope is a different physical form in which an element can exist.
qAndA.question: What is an allotrope?
What is buckminsterfullerene also known as?
